title: NAS 410 and Nadcap Audit Documentation, Cincinnati
description: Engine suppliers near Evendale: NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114 audit records prepared and reviewed for your Responsible Level 3. Send us your audit details.
h1: NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114 Audit Documentation for Cincinnati Engine Suppliers
html:
Quality managers and NDT leads at engine, component and special-process suppliers around Cincinnati use this page to plan for Nadcap assessments and engine-maker source audits. Atlantis NDT supplies the ASNT NDT Level III effort behind the paperwork: we prepare and review the NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114 audit documentation, from the written practice down to the last vision record, and your company's Responsible Level 3 approves it. To start, tell us about your audit; we reply within one business day.

Who signs what: the line between Atlantis and your Responsible Level 3

NAS 410 puts one named person in charge of a supplier's NDT qualification and certification program. That person is the Responsible Level 3, designated in writing by the employer, and the role carries approval of the written practice, course outlines, examinations, examiners and any use of an outside agency. Atlantis is not your Responsible Level 3, and we do not take that role on paper or in practice. We do not certify anyone to NAS 410, we deliver no NAS 410 training or examinations, and we never sign a certification. Your company certifies its own inspectors under its own written practice.

What we do is the work underneath those signatures. An ASNT NDT Level III from Atlantis reads your documents against NAS 410 Revision 6, the AC7114 checklists your auditor will use and the engine-maker specifications printed on your purchase orders. We mark the gaps, draft missing or weak documents in your format, clean up personnel files, run a mock audit and help you assemble corrective-action evidence after real findings. Each draft goes to your Responsible Level 3, who decides whether it is fit to approve.

The national version of this service, with the complete document list, is on the NAS 410 audit compliance documentation page. For a plain account of the standard itself, read NAS 410 explained.

The Cincinnati engine corridor and the audits it brings

Southwest Ohio is jet-engine country. GE Aerospace calls the Cincinnati area its worldwide headquarters and has produced engines at Evendale since 1949. REDI Cincinnati, the regional economic development group, counts roughly 9,000 GE Aerospace employees across about 80 facilities in southwest Ohio and northern Kentucky, the company's largest concentration of workers. In 2025 GE Aerospace announced new spending at three local sites: a ceramic matrix composite lab at Evendale, an added 3D printer and industrial furnace at West Chester, and test cell upgrades at its Peebles engine test operation.

Around that anchor sits a supply base that REDI describes as hundreds of Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers in Cincinnati and nearby Dayton. Its aerospace roster lists names such as CFM, Safran, Magellan, Meggitt, Meyer and Rhinestahl, and Barnes Aerospace has expanded in West Chester Township. Wright-Patterson Air Force Base sits up the I-75 corridor near Dayton. Across the river in Kentucky, CVG airport ranks as the sixth-largest cargo hub in the country, which keeps freighter maintenance and component repair close by.

For an NDT department, that mix produces more than one kind of auditor. A machining, coating or heat-treat house that ships engine hardware commonly holds Nadcap NDT accreditation because engine makers expect it for special processes. The same shop also hosts the prime's own supplier quality engineers, who audit against the engine maker's specifications and may watch an inspector work at the bench. Component repair shops near CVG answer to the FAA under Part 145 and to their airline customers. Defense work tied to programs managed out of Wright-Patterson can arrive with NAS 410 written into the purchase order. Each auditor opens your personnel files with a different question, and the files have to answer all of them.

Penetrant, eddy current and immersion ultrasonics on engine parts

Most NDT on engine hardware falls into three methods, and each has its own paperwork traps. Fluorescent penetrant inspection is the workhorse for blades, vanes, cases and machined details. Auditors working the penetrant slash sheet (AC7114/1) look past the certification card to the process records behind every inspection: system performance checks against a known-defect panel, UV-A intensity and ambient white-light readings at the booth, penetrant and emulsifier concentration, wash water pressure and temperature, dryer temperature and dwell times. When the inspector's certification lists one penetrant type and sensitivity level but the line runs another, that mismatch becomes a finding no matter how good the inspector is.

Eddy current carries bolt holes, blade slots, dovetails and surface scans on rotating and static parts. Here the trouble is usually traceability. Each reference standard needs a serial number and a certificate, each technique needs to name the probe and instrument settings the Level 3 approved, and each inspector's certification has to cover the techniques actually used. Immersion ultrasonics on disks, shafts and forgings has its own slash sheet for rotating components, and the records it expects are heavy: tank and system checks, reference block certifications, scan plans by part number and evidence that the specific examination tested the part families the inspector signs for.

Atlantis reviews those technique documents and the personnel files that point to them as one package, so a technique change that never reached the certification records surfaces before the auditor finds it. Method background for local teams is on the penetrant testing in Cincinnati, eddy current testing in Cincinnati and ultrasonic testing in Cincinnati pages, and the procedure side is covered under AC7114 NDT procedures.

Ceramic matrix composites and additive parts: new techniques, new records

GE Aerospace's investment in a ceramic matrix composite lab and in more additive capacity tells local suppliers where engine hardware is heading. New materials bring inspection techniques that may not exist yet in a supplier's written practice. A shop that adds a technique has to decide how inspectors are trained in it, what the specific and practical examinations contain, how experience in that technique is logged and who approves the technique sheet. Until those answers are written down and approved, an inspector cannot be certified for the technique, however much time they have spent on it in development.

This is careful work rather than fast work. We draft technique sheets, qualification plans and demonstration records for the Responsible Level 3 to review, using the structure on our procedure qualification and demonstration page. We can also help write the technique instructions themselves through NDT procedure development. Computed tomography of additive parts is a radiographic technique, and radiography is work Atlantis never performs on US soil. Reviewing the CT or film procedure documents, and the personnel records behind them, remains within what a Level III from Atlantis can do.

What a Nadcap NDT auditor samples in an engine supplier's files

An auditor working the AC7114 baseline checklist does not read every file. They pull the personnel list, choose names, and compare each chosen file against your written practice and the customer requirements it was written to meet. The table below shows where Cincinnati engine suppliers most often come up short.

RecordWhat the auditor compares it withWhere engine-hardware shops slip
Written practiceNAS 410 Revision 6 and every prime specification on active ordersStill cites Revision 5, or omits a technique the line now uses
Responsible Level 3 designationA dated, signed appointment by the employerThe named person left, and nobody updated the letter
Training recordsApproved course outline, hours by method and level, qualified instructorHours logged with no outline attached, or an instructor with no recorded qualification
Experience recordsDated entries by method, signed by a certified supervisorOne summary line written on certification day
Vision recordsNear vision at least every 12 months, plus color perceptionColor check done at hire and never repeated where the practice requires it
ExaminationsGeneral, specific and practical papers, keys and gradingPapers discarded after the score was copied into a spreadsheet
Outside-agency agreementsScope and approval by the Responsible Level 3A training vendor used for years with no written agreement

The examination row deserves extra attention, and the AC7114 examination records guide explains what to keep. Vision, experience and training files each have their own page: vision examination records, experience logs and training records and certificates. For a wider look at assessor habits, see Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness and what Nadcap accreditation actually checks.

Revision 6 and the long-tenured Level 2

NAS 410 Revision 6 was released by AIA, with Accuris as distributor, in December 2025. AIA highlighted two changes: clarified certification requirements and a new Appendix D route to Level 3, under which Level 2 personnel earn points for designated NDT activities before sitting the initial Level 3 examination. Work from the standard itself rather than from summaries, including ours, because the detail is in the text.

The points route matters in a region like this one, where many engine shops have Level 2 inspectors with long careers on one product line. Whether that history counts depends on records. If years of technique development, procedure drafting or trainee supervision were never logged against a person's name, the Responsible Level 3 has little to credit. When your Responsible Level 3 has decided how the company will use Appendix D, we can help organize existing records into the categories the written practice adopts. Timing of the move to Revision 6 is set by your customers and your written practice; check the transition wording in the standard and any date a prime has published, then change the written practice, training material and examination banks together. The NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A comparison is useful if your staff also hold ASNT-based certifications for non-aerospace work.

Remote and on-site support across the Tri-State

Atlantis works from Houston and Hyderabad and travels to Ohio, Kentucky and Indiana sites when the job needs someone in the room. Much of the work runs remotely: you share documents through your own secure system, we return a gap report and marked-up drafts, and we talk through each finding with the quality manager and the Responsible Level 3. Site visits suit three tasks best: auditing personnel files at the source, walking the penetrant line or ultrasonic tank with the process records in hand, and running a mock audit that sounds and feels like the real one, including interviews with inspectors.

Some suppliers here run both aerospace work and industrial work, such as power-generation or process-plant parts, under different certification documents. Keeping the two programs separate on paper is part of the job. For the wider regional picture, see aerospace NDT in Cincinnati and NDT consulting in Ohio. If inspectors need method training, Atlantis teaches courses built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, described on the aerospace NDT training page. Whether any outside course counts within a NAS 410 program is decided by the employer's Responsible Level 3, not by the course provider.

How an engagement runs

  1. Scoping call. We agree the audit type (Nadcap, prime source audit, FAA or customer), the date, the methods and the documents in scope.
  2. Gap review. A Level III checks your written practice, technique sheets and a handful of personnel files line by line against the Revision 6 text, the Nadcap baseline and method checklists, and each engine-maker specification on open orders.
  3. Drafting. We write or revise documents in your format and terminology, each marked for Responsible Level 3 review.
  4. Record clean-up. We list every file defect by person and record type so your team can fix originals; we never backdate or recreate signatures.
  5. Mock audit. We run the checklist the way an assessor would and write up what we find.
  6. After the audit. If findings arrive, we help with root cause and the corrective-action evidence your response needs, as described in aerospace NDT corrective actions.

What to send us before a Cincinnati audit

  • The current written practice and its revision history.
  • The Responsible Level 3 designation and any outside-agency agreements.
  • The list of prime specifications on active purchase orders that touch NDT.
  • Your personnel roster by method, level and technique, with certification and vision dates.
  • Two or three complete personnel files, ideally a recent hire, a long-tenured inspector and a Level 3.
  • Technique sheets for the parts that ship most often, plus the process-control logs for one recent month.
  • Your last audit report and its corrective-action responses, if you have them.

If your files live in a software system, an export works. Suppliers moving away from spreadsheets can see how certificates and expiry dates are tracked in Atlantis ERP certificates, and why records scatter before audits in the audit evidence scramble.

A short readiness checklist for engine-hardware NDT shops

  1. The written practice names Revision 6, or a dated plan explains when it will.
  2. Every technique on the shop floor appears in the written practice and on at least one certification.
  3. Each penetrant line has a month of complete process-control records with no blank shifts.
  4. Every reference standard used for eddy current or ultrasonics has a current certificate on file.
  5. No inspector's vision record is older than the interval the written practice sets.
  6. Examination papers, keys and practical checklists are kept, not just the scores.
  7. Outside agencies, including any instructor or examiner from outside the company, have a signed scope approved by the Responsible Level 3.
  8. Any finding from the last audit has closed evidence that a stranger could follow.

faq.q: Can Atlantis act as our Responsible Level 3?
faq.a: No. Atlantis does not accept the Responsible Level 3 role. The employer puts that appointment in writing, and the person can be on the payroll or engaged from an outside agency. What we hand over are drafts and review notes, which stay drafts until your Responsible Level 3 approves them.

faq.q: Do you certify our inspectors to NAS 410?
faq.a: No. Certification under NAS 410 belongs to your company, issued through its written practice. Atlantis does not certify anyone, does not run NAS 410 examinations and does not deliver NAS 410 training. We test whether the evidence in each file would justify the certificate you signed.

faq.q: We supply an engine maker with its own NDT specifications. Do those replace NAS 410?
faq.a: Usually they sit on top of it. A prime specification often invokes NAS 410 and adds its own requirements, such as approved techniques or examinations on specific part families. We build a flow-down matrix so the written practice answers every document on your active orders.

faq.q: Our last Nadcap audit was against Revision 5. What changes for Revision 6?
faq.a: Start with the Revision 6 text and any transition date your engine customers publish, and revise the written practice, course material and exam question banks in one controlled release. AIA highlights clarified certification requirements and a new Appendix D points route to Level 3. See NAS 410 explained for the summary.

faq.q: What does the penetrant slash sheet auditor look at besides certifications?
faq.a: Process control. Expect questions about system performance checks, UV-A and white-light readings, concentration checks, wash and dryer settings, and whether each inspection traces to an approved technique. Missing shifts in the log are a common finding.

faq.q: Can you help after we have already received Nadcap findings?
faq.a: Yes. We help with root cause, the corrective action and the objective evidence for your response. The supplier writes and submits the response; we review it before it goes. See aerospace NDT corrective actions.

faq.q: Do you come to Evendale, West Chester or Dayton, or is the work remote?
faq.a: Both. Document review and drafting usually run remotely, and a Level III travels to your site for file audits, process walk-throughs and the mock audit. Atlantis works from Houston and Hyderabad and has no Ohio office.

faq.q: Our component repair shop near CVG works under Part 145. Does NAS 410 apply?
faq.a: Only if a contract, customer requirement or manual invokes it. Part 145 requires a training program and inspection personnel the FAA accepts, and many airline customers add NAS 410. See Part 145 repair station NDT.

faq.q: Will you perform radiography or CT on our additive parts?
faq.a: No. In the United States, Atlantis performs no radiographic work of any kind, CT included. Reviewing radiographic procedures and the related personnel files can still be part of the documentation scope.

faq.q: Do you hold Nadcap accreditation or prime approvals?
faq.a: No. Atlantis holds no Nadcap accreditation and no prime approvals. Atlantis is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 14001. The accreditation in a Nadcap audit is yours; our job is to help your documents hold up.
